readback_body:
## Description

**P0 — macOS v1.0.0 Agent crashes with SIGBUS after successful startup and registration.** Treat as a release-blocking native runtime defect for the next patch candidate, not an installer/download failure. A real user reports the issue on macOS ARM64 after upgrading from v0.x. Agent identity and tmux inventory were loaded; the Agent registered successfully, then the foreground process exited with a bus error near its initial heartbeat.

## Reproduction

Observed on 2026-11-26, macOS ARM64, release 1.0.0:

```text
$ nession agent start -f
INFO nession_agent::runtime: nession-agent 1.0.0 starting
INFO nession_agent::runtime: tmux is available
INFO nession_agent::runtime: Agent WebSocket server started
INFO nession_agent::connection::server_client: registration accepted: Registration successful
INFO nession_agent::runtime: Connected to central server (heartbeat interval: 10s)
INFO nession_agent::runtime: Heartbeat loop started (interval: 10s)
INFO nession_agent::runtime: Session watcher started (interval: 5s)
INFO nession_agent::runtime: Git invalidation watcher started
INFO nession_agent::netwatch::platform: SCDynamicStore run loop started on dedicated thread
INFO nession_agent::sync::heartbeat: Sending heartbeat: sessions=106, active=0, uptime=0s
[1] 42386 bus error nession agent start -f
```

User-specific paths, endpoints, and identity omitted. Do not require destroying real sessions to reproduce. Use an isolated test home/socket, local test Server and disposable tmux sessions. Reproduce with small and 106-session inventories; exercise process discovery explicitly during and after registration. Collect a sanitized macOS .ips or LLDB crash thread/backtrace if available. Last emitted log is not proof of the crashing thread.

## Investigation Status

**Confirmed source defect:** both [v1.0.0 macos.rs](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/v1.0.0/crates/nession-agent/src/session/process_discovery/macos.rs) and current main at investigation time use the following in `rusage`:

```rust
let mut info: libc::rusage_info_v4 = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
let mut pointer: libc::rusage_info_t = (&mut info as *mut libc::rusage_info_v4).cast();
let result = unsafe {
    libc::proc_pid_rusage(pid as libc::c_int, libc::RUSAGE_INFO_V4, &mut pointer)
};
```

The C ABI takes the address of the actual output storage (despite the pointer-to-pointer-shaped declaration in libc bindings). Passing the address of the local pointer slot instead of the structure buffer allows the native implementation to write a full rusage record into pointer-sized storage, risking stack corruption and undefined behavior. Confirm the pinned libc binding and Apple libproc ABI before changing the cast. This defect is independent of the reported crash's exact trigger and must be fixed.

**Not yet proven:** this FFI defect caused the reported SIGBUS. No crash report/backtrace is available. Heartbeat's macOS uptime/load functions return defaults and the send path constructs a protocol frame; SessionWatcher skips the immediate tick and several tasks are concurrent. Trace actual invocation paths (including incoming process-discovery requests), do not assume the final heartbeat log caused the crash. Also inspect SCDynamicStore callback lifetimes and other native FFI reachable from startup; investigate any residual SIGBUS after correcting rusage. Do not claim a reproduced root cause without native evidence.

## Impact

Agent becomes unavailable after successful registration; existing tmux Sessions may survive but remote control, Session synchronization and capability operations become unavailable. A successful readiness notification or first heartbeat is insufficient release evidence. The rusage defect also threatens on-demand Agent process metrics whenever invoked. No data corruption or credential exposure has been observed; avoid unsubstantiated claims.

## Fix Direction

- Correct `proc_pid_rusage` to pass the address of properly aligned, full-sized `rusage_info_v4` storage, cast directly to the exact argument type of the pinned libc binding; do not pass `&mut pointer`. Document the ABI and safety invariant; validate return/error handling and preserve honest metric states.
- Review adjacent macOS unsafe boundaries (libproc buffers/sizes, sysctl, devname lifetime, network watcher callbacks) for equivalent pointer, size, alignment and lifetime mistakes. Fix proven related defects at their existing owners. No blanket unsafe suppressions, no new process-discovery owner.
- Add native macOS regression tests with same-user disposable child processes, repeated real rusage sampling and explicit failed/vanished PID cases. Verify actual output fields and monotonic counters where meaningful, not merely survival or successful compilation. Use a subprocess boundary for fault diagnostics and sanitizer coverage where supported.
- Add bounded native release-mode startup/runtime coverage for real CLI and standalone Agent: isolated home/tmux socket, existing Session inventory including 106-session case, registration, repeated heartbeats, explicit process snapshots, reconnect and clean shutdown. Confirm no SIGBUS/SIGSEGV, no Session loss and no unintended host tmux cleanup. Use the canonical quality/acceptance owners and macOS runner already used in release-production; add a narrowly scoped exact-SHA native test job as needed, not a new competing workflow system. Require target-architecture execution, not cross-compilation alone. Preserve Linux behavior.
- Make native runtime proof a prerequisite for the affected macOS release candidate; publish crash diagnostics on failure with redaction, not credentials or raw terminal contents. If an Intel runner is unavailable, track that proof separately as Pending, never infer it from ARM64 or Linux.
- Non-goals: redesign installation/upgrade, disable process discovery/heartbeats/network watching as a permanent workaround, change protocol/UI, delete real tmux Sessions or user data, or automatically deploy a patch.

## Location

- `crates/nession-agent/src/session/process_discovery/macos.rs`: `rusage`, `sample`, `details`
- `crates/nession-agent/src/session/process_discovery/mod.rs`: platform dispatch
- `crates/nession-agent/src/runtime.rs`, `sync/heartbeat.rs`, `sync/session_watcher.rs`, `netwatch.rs`, `connection/server_client.rs`: diagnosis and runtime coverage
- `crates/nession-cli/src/commands/agent/start.rs`: foreground runtime entry
- `.github/workflows/release-production.yml`: existing macOS build runner and release evidence boundary
- Related original process-discovery contract: #2514; runtime readiness: #1016; network watcher: #91; Session Activity: #3800/#3802. This is a distinct native memory-safety defect, not a replacement of those requirements.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 Native macOS process discovery writes rusage output into valid structure-sized storage; real repeated same-user child sampling produces valid resource counters and handles vanished/denied processes without invalid writes, process crash or fabricated zero metrics. Exact-head native Rust regression proves the original boundary and the correction.
- [ ] SC-02 On native macOS ARM64, release-mode Agent startup with isolated existing tmux inventories of at least 1 and 106 Sessions, a real local Server and explicit process-discovery requests remains alive across at least three heartbeat intervals, publishes expected Session inventory, survives reconnect, and shuts down cleanly without losing Sessions or touching non-owned tmux resources. Capture exit/signal status and sanitized diagnostics.
- [ ] SC-03 The affected macOS release build cannot report successful runtime qualification for an exact candidate SHA without the native startup and rusage regression receipts; failed native tests block the affected candidate, and unsupported/missing native execution stays visibly Pending, not a cross-build-derived Pass. Linux process-discovery regression stays green.
- [x] SC-04 Investigation records the actual observed crash thread/function if a reproducible native SIGBUS or user report is available, documents the verified FFI defect separately from the incident attribution, and records review of adjacent unsafe boundaries plus any unresolved diagnostic limitations. No claim of incident root cause without evidence.

**SC → scenario / proof:** SC-01/02 → SCN-03 (native runtime profile; no elevated privileges needed), exact PR SHA native ARM64 Rust test and isolated release-mode Agent/Server/tmux fixture on approved GitHub-hosted macOS runner; capture OS/arch, actual signal/exit, counter observations, Session counts, heartbeat receipts and teardown. SC-03 → SCN-05, exact-head workflow/Gate negative and positive checks plus authenticated native job receipts; target existing release macOS runner, with required native PR check before promotion. SC-04 → SCN-01, exact-head source audit and recorded diagnostic evidence/limitations. Native lane exists for builds; adding execution coverage is part of this fix, Pending until independently executed. No production credentials or broad host privileges required. Verification tier integration, not an all-system Full Regression requirement for this narrow PR.
